title: Visitor and Cellar
premise: August Quintana hosts a dead-of-night radio show from a house they inherited from their grandmother, taking calls from listeners who all died the week before. When the sleep recordings meant to capture the house's haunting instead capture a second voice answering August's questions, they learn the house is a cell that keeps something fed through ritual song, and that their grandmother was its jailer, not its victim. The voice, a drowned girl named Wren, offers August love and escape in exchange for singing the song's last verse, which would open the cellar door and free what's inside. In the end August sings the verse alone, taking the jailer's place willingly, and Wren, choosing love against duty, stays to share the sentence, the two of them keeping the lights on together.
about_author: Juniper Zhou is a former late-night radio producer who spent three years on the overnight shift and never quite shook the habit of talking to empty rooms. They write horror about houses that remember, and live in a coastal town where the fog comes in on schedule.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: August's POV. Introduces the nightly broadcast from the inherited house, where every caller is someone who died last week. August keeps strict rituals: lights on, doors counted, never after midnight. Emotional beat: lonely competence masking dread, and the first hint that the calls are coming from inside the house.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: August's POV. Sorting their grandmother's papers, August finds a hymnal with the last verse torn out and a deed with a strange condition: the radio must broadcast nightly. A lawyer's letter warns against 'answering questions after dark.' Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion about who their grandmother really was.

chapters.title: Sleep Study
chapters.summary: August's POV. Hoping to document the haunting, August records themselves sleeping. Playback reveals a second voice in the room answering questions August murmured in dreams. The voice is patient, curious, and knows August's grandmother's name. Emotional beat: violation and fascination tangled together.

chapters.title: Wren, Under the Floor
chapters.summary: August's POV. The voice identifies itself as Wren, drowned in the cellar cistern in 1961, and claims she's a prisoner too. She teaches August the house's rules and warns them about the song. Emotional beat: the dangerous tenderness of the only company August has ever trusted.

chapters.title: Verse by Verse
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between August and Wren's memories. Wren shows how the song works: three verses bind the thing below, the fourth was never meant to be sung. August realizes the dead callers are the song's previous singers, still calling for help. Emotional beat: mounting horror as duty's true shape emerges.

chapters.title: The Listeners
chapters.summary: August's POV. A caller who died this week, not last, begs August to sing the last verse and end it. The dead callers turn hostile when August refuses, overrunning the switchboard, reciting the first three verses in unison. Emotional beat: siege, isolation, the temptation to surrender.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Kept
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Flashback: Wren's love for the young jailer who came before, and how she chose the cell over escape, and was drowned for it. August finds the torn verse hidden in a photograph frame. Emotional beat: Wren's guilt, and love revealed as the trap's original bait.

chapters.title: Count the Doors
chapters.summary: August's POV. The house begins uncounting itself: doors appear where walls were, lights die room by room. The thing below speaks in August's dead mother's voice, offering a bargain. August nearly sings, stopped only by Wren screaming through the floorboards. Emotional beat: rock-bottom terror and betrayal.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: Climax. August descends to the cellar door with the hymnal, Wren's voice guiding them. To renew the binding, the verse must be sung by a willing jailer. August sings it alone, feeling the cell close around them, and understands their grandmother's choice at last. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into love.

chapters.title: Visitor and Cellar
chapters.summary: Resolution, Wren's POV. The show goes on, hosted by a voice the dead callers finally trust. Wren breaks her own duty and stays in the cell with August rather than take their place and leave. Two voices now answer the sleep recordings, keeping the lights on together. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace, a sentence shared.
